mainTopic: שפחה חרופה: who she is, how her lashes and the man's אשם are linked, and how her laws differ from other עריות
overview: This amud finishes the משנה about שפחה חרופה, a maidservant designated for a man, and records a מחלוקת about who exactly she is. The גמרא learns from the words בקורת תהיה that only she gets lashes, and רבי יצחק and רב אשי explain why בקורת means lashes. רבא shows from the order of the פסוק that the man brings his אשם only when she is lashed, and the word 'אשמו' shows that only he brings it. רבי יצחק adds that the man is liable only if she was not a virgin, learning from the word נחרפת. רב חסדא ties this law to the כהנים in עזרא who brought a ram as an אשם. A ברייתא then lays out four views of who she is: רבי עקיבא, רבי ישמעאל, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה and אחרים. The גמרא explains the source behind each view. A new משנה teaches that in all עריות each partner is judged separately, and רב יהודה explains that with a שפחה חרופה, if one partner is exempt, both are exempt. Finally רב ששת challenges a ברייתא that treats four pairs of cases as equal, and that discussion continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The deliberate sinner is treated like the accidental one
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of ways שפחה חרופה is unusual: a deliberate sinner is treated like an accidental one.
steps.simpleTranslation: With a שפחה חרופה, the Torah treated someone who sins on purpose the same as someone who sins by mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the end of a משנה sentence. It lists ways the שפחה חרופה case differs from all other forbidden relationships, and this is the last item.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With other עריות, only a שוגג (accidental sinner) brings a קרבן; a מזיד (deliberate sinner) gets a harsher punishment. Here, both the מזיד and the שוגג bring the same קרבן אשם.

keyTerms.meaning: A maidservant designated (partly betrothed) to a Jewish man

steps.confusionAlert: This is the tail end of a longer sentence that began before this section. The 'her' is the שפחה חרופה.

phrases.english: that He made, regarding her, the intentional sinner like the unintentional one.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the Torah. With her, both kinds of sinner bring the same קרבן אשם.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes a list in the משנה that began before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For שפחה חרופה, the deliberate and the accidental sinner are treated the same (both bring an אשם).

steps.title: רבי יהודה: she is half-maidservant, half-free
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה defines שפחה חרופה as a woman who is half slave and half free, based on the פסוק 'redeemed, not redeemed'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Which maidservant is meant? Any woman who is half maidservant and half free, because the פסוק says 'and redeemed she was not redeemed.' This is רבי יהודה's view.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks which maidservant the Torah means. רבי יהודה answers that she is someone only partly freed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה reads the double phrase 'redeemed, not redeemed' as describing someone halfway: partly redeemed and partly not. For example, she had two owners and one of them freed his half.

keyTerms.meaning: Half of her is a maidservant
'And redeemed, she was not redeemed' (the פסוק's wording)

phrases.english: Which maidservant?
Any woman who is half maidservant
and half a free woman,
as it is said: "And redeemed, she was not redeemed",
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20. רבי יהודה reads it as half redeemed, half not.

phrases.english: These are the words of Rabbi Yehuda.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the laws of שפחה חרופה to defining who she is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, שפחה חרופה is a woman who is half slave and half free.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: she is a full maidservant
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל disagrees and says the פסוק speaks of a complete maidservant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: this is a definite, complete maidservant.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל argues with רבי יהודה about who the שפחה חרופה is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, the double wording 'redeemed, not redeemed' is just the Torah's way of saying she was not redeemed at all. So she is fully a slave, not half free.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
This is a definite maidservant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רבי יהודה's definition.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי ישמעאל, שפחה חרופה is a full maidservant.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: the only case left is the half-free maidservant
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב argues that every other forbidden relationship is already spelled out in the Torah, so this law must be about the half-free maidservant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: all the forbidden relationships are already written out clearly. The only case left over is a woman who is half maidservant and half free.
steps.whatsHappening: A third תנא gives a reason that supports the half-free definition. His reasoning is that no other case is left for this law to cover.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A full maidservant is not covered by the ordinary laws of עריות, and a fully free married woman is already covered by the law of אשת איש. The only 'gap' the Torah has not covered is the half-free woman, so the פסוק of שפחה חרופה must be filling that gap.

keyTerms.meaning: A leftover case, something not yet covered

steps.whatToRemember: There are three views on who is a שפחה חרופה. רבי יהודה says she is half-free, based on the פסוק. רבי ישמעאל says she is a full maidservant. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says she is half-free, because that is the only case left uncovered.

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov says:
All forbidden relationships are spelled out,
and we have no leftover case

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא חֶצְיָהּ שִׁפְחָה וְחֶצְיָהּ בַּת חוֹרִין.
phrases.english: except one who is half maidservant and half free woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת מְפוֹרָשׁוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a third view, which agrees with רבי יהודה's outcome for a different reason.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שפחה חרופה must be the half-free woman, since that is the only case the Torah's other laws leave uncovered.

steps.title: How do we know only she gets lashes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking for the source that the woman receives lashes and the man does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: From where do we know that she is lashed and he is not lashed?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and asks for the source behind a rule from the משנה: in this case, only the woman is lashed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually in עריות, both partners receive the same punishment. Here the משנה says the man is not treated like the woman, so the גמרא wants to see where the Torah teaches this difference. This step sets up the answer that comes next.

phrases.english: GEMARA
From where do we know that she is lashed
phrases.notes: The letter in square brackets is added in the corrected wording.

phrases.english: and he is not lashed?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָלַן דְּהִיא לָקְיָא וְהוּא לָא לָקֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of a rule in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The Torah source showing that only the woman, and not the man, receives lashes.

steps.title: The ברייתא learns it from 'בקורת תהיה'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns lashes from the word בקורת, and learns that only she is lashed from the feminine verb תהיה.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: 'There shall be בקורת' teaches that she is lashed. You might think both are lashed, so the Torah says 'תהיה', a feminine verb: she is lashed, and he is not lashed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with a ברייתא that reads two words from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word בקורת tells us there are lashes. The verb תהיה ('she shall be') is feminine, which limits the lashes to the woman alone.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק's word for her punishment, here understood as lashes
'One might think…', which introduces a possible mistaken idea
'The Torah teaches', introducing the word that disproves it

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"There shall be בקורת"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20

phrases.english: teaches that she is lashed.
One might think both of them are lashed?
The verse says: "she shall be"
phrases.notes: The verb is feminine, so it points only to the woman.

phrases.english: she is lashed and he is not lashed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בקורת teaches that there are lashes, and the feminine תהיה limits them to the woman.

steps.title: Why does 'בקורת' mean lashes?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know that the word בקורת refers to lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from where do we know that this word בקורת is a word that means lashes?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא assumed that בקורת means lashes. Now the גמרא asks what that assumption is based on, which sets up the next two answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Plainly, בקורת sounds like 'inspection' or 'examination', not like 'whipping'. So the גמרא wants a link between this word and מלקות.

phrases.english: And from where do we know that this "בקורת"
is a word meaning lashes?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִנַּיִן דְּהָדֵין בִּקּוֹרֶת לִישָּׁנָא דְּמַלְקוּת הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions an assumption built into the ברייתא of step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the word בקורת should be understood as lashes.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: 'בקורת' points to the reading of פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק connects בקורת to קריאה, the reading of פסוקים that goes along with lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: it means 'she shall be with the readings.' As a ברייתא teaches: the greatest of the judges reads the פסוקים aloud, the second counts the lashes, and the third says 'Strike him!'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק answers by hearing the word בקורת as related to 'reading' (קריאה). Reading פסוקים aloud is part of the lashing procedure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: While lashes are given, one judge reads פסוקים aloud. So a word that suggests 'reading' points to the lashing procedure. A ברייתא describing the three judges' jobs proves that reading is part of it.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
"She shall be with the readings",
phrases.notes: He hears בקורת as sounding like קריאה, reading.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a ברייתא:
the greatest of the judges reads aloud,
the second counts,
the third says: Strike him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בקורת relates to קריאה, the reading of פסוקים that is part of lashes.

steps.title: רב אשי: 'בקורת' points to the assessment before lashes
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי connects בקורת to ביקור, the assessment of how many lashes the person can handle.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי says: it means 'she shall be under assessment.' As the משנה teaches: they assess him only by a number of lashes that can be divided into three.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי gives a different link. He hears בקורת as ביקור, the 'checking' or assessment done before lashes are given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before lashes, the court checks how many the person can take, and that number must divide by three. Since this assessment is part of the lashing procedure, a word meaning 'checking' points to lashes.
steps.whatToRemember: Only the שפחה חרופה gets lashes, as the ברייתא learns from the feminine תהיה. The word בקורת points to lashes either through the reading of פסוקים (רבי יצחק) or through the assessment beforehand (רב אשי).

phrases.english: Rav Ashi says:
"She shall be under assessment",
as we learned in a משנה:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה in מכות 22a.

phrases.english: they do not assess him
except by lashes fit to be divided into three.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different answer to the question of step 7 than רבי יצחק gave.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: בקורת relates to ביקור, the court's assessment of how many lashes the person can take.

steps.title: The man's offering depends on the woman's lashes
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא rules that the man brings a קרבן only in a case where the woman is lashed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: whenever the woman is lashed, the man brings an offering. When the woman is not lashed, the man does not bring an offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that ties the man's קרבן to the woman's lashes. If she gets lashes, he brings the offering, and if she does not, he does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Up to now we learned that she gets lashes and he does not. This ברייתא adds a new rule: the two punishments go together. His offering only comes into play when her lashes do.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering; here the man's קרבן אשם

phrases.english: The Sages taught: At the time that the woman is lashed,
the man brings an offering;
if the woman is not lashed,
the man does not bring an offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new rule that links her lashes, already established, to his offering.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man brings a קרבן only when the woman is lashed.

steps.title: Asking for the source of the link
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that his offering depends on her lashes.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the ברייתא's rule. This sets up רבא's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gave a rule but no פסוק. The גמרא wants to know which פסוק ties the two punishments together.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it? A request for a source

phrases.english: From where do we derive this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא's rule.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that makes the man's offering depend on the woman's lashes.

steps.title: רבא quotes the פסוק of שפחה חרופה
steps.stepSummary: רבא begins his answer by quoting the opening of the פסוק about שפחה חרופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: It is written: 'And if a man lies carnally with a woman, and she is a maidservant designated for a man, and she was not redeemed, nor was freedom given to her.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבא starts his answer by quoting the פסוק. The real proof comes in the next steps, where he looks at the order of the words that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This פסוק describes the case of a שפחה חרופה. Right after it, the תורה says 'בקורת תהיה' and only then 'והביא את אשמו'. רבא will build his proof on that order.

keyTerms.meaning: A maidservant designated (betrothed) to a man; the שפחה חרופה
She was not fully redeemed; she is still partly a slave
Freedom; she was not set free

phrases.english: Rava said: As it is written:

phrases.aramaic: ״וְאִישׁ כִּי יִשְׁכַּב אֶת אִשָּׁה שִׁכְבַת זֶרַע
phrases.english: "And if a man lies carnally with a woman,
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20. The next פסוק goes on with 'בקורת תהיה' and 'והביא את אשמו', which רבא is about to use.

phrases.english: and she is a maidservant designated for a man,
and she was not at all redeemed,
nor was freedom given to her."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to מנלן by quoting the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The source is the passage about שפחה חרופה in ויקרא 19:20 and 21.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק put the lashes before the offering?
steps.stepSummary: Since the פסוק is talking about the man, it should have mentioned his offering first. So why does it mention her lashes first?
steps.simpleTranslation: Since up to here the פסוק is talking about the man, it should have written 'He shall bring his guilt offering to ה׳' first, and 'There shall be an inspection' at the end. Why did the תורה write 'There shall be an inspection' first and 'He shall bring his guilt offering' after?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא points out that the order of the פסוק looks strange. This question sets up the answer that gives the source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק opens by talking about the man, so we would expect it to stay with him and speak about his offering. Instead it first mentions her lashes and only then his offering. That unusual order must be teaching something.

keyTerms.meaning: Since, after all; it opens a point both sides agree on
Is speaking about, is dealing with
'The Merciful One', meaning the תורה or ה׳
A guilt offering, the man's קרבן here

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדִי עַד הָכָא בְּאִישׁ קָא מִשְׁתַּעֵי קְרָא,
phrases.english: Since until here the verse is speaking about the man,
let it write: "He shall bring his guilt offering to ה׳,"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:21

phrases.english: and at the end let it write: "There shall be an inspection."
phrases.notes: Remember from the earlier steps: 'בקורת' means her lashes.

phrases.english: Why did the Merciful One write first: "There shall be an inspection,"
and at the end write: "He shall bring his guilt offering to ה׳"?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִכְּדִי עַד הָכָא בְּאִישׁ קָא מִשְׁתַּעֵי קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Looks at the order of the פסוק that רבא just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the unusual order of the פסוק, lashes before offering, comes to teach.

steps.title: His offering depends on her lashes
steps.stepSummary: The order teaches a condition: if she is lashed, he brings an אשם, and if she is not, he does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what it means: if there will be an inspection (she is lashed), then he brings his guilt offering. If there will not be an inspection, he does not bring his guilt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא explains that the order of the פסוק works like an 'if... then' sentence. This finishes the source for the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By putting her lashes first, the פסוק makes his offering the result of her lashes. So whenever she is not lashed, he brings no offering at all. This is exactly what the ברייתא said.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means; it reads the text in a new way
'There shall be an inspection', meaning she is lashed

steps.whatToRemember: The man's אשם depends on the woman's lashes. That is why the פסוק says 'בקורת תהיה' before 'והביא את אשמו'.

phrases.english: This is what it is saying:
If there will be an inspection for her,
"he shall bring his guilt offering to ה׳";
but if there will not be an inspection,
he shall not bring his guilt offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question about the order of the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The order makes the man's offering depend on the woman's lashes.

steps.title: Maybe the woman also brings an offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the פסוק only kept him from lashes, and that she should get lashes and also bring an offering.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say that the פסוק only left him out of the lashes, but she should be lashed and also bring an offering!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that only the man brings the offering. Maybe the woman gets lashes and also brings a קרבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the word 'תהיה' was used to keep the man out of the lashes. But that only tells us he gets no lashes. It says nothing to stop her from bringing a קרבן as well.

keyTerms.meaning: Say, suggest; it offers another way to read the text

phrases.english: Say that the verse left him out (of the lashes),
phrases.notes: This points back to step 6, where 'תהיה' taught that only she is lashed.

phrases.english: but she should be lashed and also bring an offering!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the idea that only the man brings the offering.
steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the woman brings no קרבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק only kept the man out of the lashes. Nothing yet keeps the woman out of the offering.

steps.title: 'His' offering means only he brings it
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'אשמו', his guilt offering, which shows that only the man brings it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'He shall bring his guilt offering to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word 'his' in the פסוק limits the offering to the man alone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה could have just said 'he shall bring a guilt offering'. It wrote 'his guilt offering' instead, which shows the offering belongs only to the man. So she gets lashes and no קרבן.

keyTerms.meaning: His guilt offering; the word 'his' limits it to the man

steps.whatToRemember: The man brings the קרבן and the woman gets the lashes. Each gets only one of the two.

phrases.english: "He shall bring his guilt offering to ה׳" is written.
phrases.notes: The point is the word 'his'. It is his offering, not hers.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא with a close reading of the פסוק.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Close reading of one word in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: She might be lashed and also bring an offering.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word 'אשמו' (his) shows that only the man brings the offering.

steps.title: רבי יצחק: liable only with a non-virgin שפחה
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק teaches that the man is liable only if the שפחה already had relations before, learning it from the word 'נחרפת'.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק said: Actually, a man is liable only for a maidservant who is not a virgin, as it says: 'And she is a maidservant designated (נחרפת) for a man.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יצחק adds a new limit to this law. The man is liable only when the שפחה חרופה was already not a virgin.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a new point about which case the law covers. רבי יצחק reads the word 'נחרפת' as telling us that she was already changed from her first state. The next steps explain why the word means that.

keyTerms.meaning: Actually, really; it introduces a firm rule
A maidservant who already had relations, not a virgin

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak said:
Actually, he is liable only
for a maidservant who is not a virgin,
as it is stated: "And she is a maidservant designated for a man."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק: לְעוֹלָם אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new point: which שפחה makes the man liable.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The man is liable for a שפחה חרופה only if she was already not a virgin.

steps.title: How do we know 'נחרפת' means change?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how we know the word 'נחרפת' speaks about a change.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we see that this word 'נחרפת' is a word of change?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for proof of רבי יצחק's reading. This sets up the two proofs that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק's rule only works if 'נחרפת' means 'changed', meaning she is no longer a virgin. So the גמרא needs to show where the word is used that way.

keyTerms.meaning: How do we see it? From where is it shown?

phrases.english: And from where is it shown
that this word "designated" is a term of change?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for proof of רבי יצחק's reading of 'נחרפת'.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Proof that the word 'נחרפת' means change.

steps.title: Proof from הריפות in שמואל
steps.stepSummary: The word הריפות (crushed grain) in שמואל ב shows that the root means something changed from its first form.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And she spread crushed grain (הריפות) over it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves the meaning of the word from a פסוק in שמואל ב that uses the same root.
steps.deeperAnalysis: הריפות is grain that has been crushed, so it was changed from its first form. Since 'נחרפת' shares this root, it also speaks about a change. Here that means she is no longer a virgin.

keyTerms.meaning: Crushed grain, grain changed from its first form

phrases.english: As it is written: "And she spread crushed grain over it."
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 17:19

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question with a פסוק that uses the same root.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הריפות means crushed grain, so the root speaks about change.

steps.title: Second proof from הריפות in משלי
steps.stepSummary: Another option: the פסוק in משלי about pounding grain in a mortar, using the same word הריפות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say it comes from: 'Even if you pound a fool in a mortar with a pestle among the crushed grain (הריפות).'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second פסוק that shows the same meaning of the word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here הריפות is clearly grain being pounded in a mortar, so it is changed from its first form. This proves the same point a second way: 'נחרפת' is a word of change.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say; it brings a second option
A mortar, a bowl for pounding

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יצחק: the man is liable only for a שפחה חרופה who is not a virgin. 'נחרפת' means changed, like הריפות, crushed grain.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
"Though you pound the fool in a mortar
phrases.notes: משלי 27:22

phrases.english: among the crushed grain with a pestle."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second proof for the same meaning of the word.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: הריפות in משלי is grain pounded in a mortar, so the root means change.

steps.title: The כהנים in עזרא brought guilt offerings for designated maidservants
steps.stepSummary: רב חסדא reads the פסוק in עזרא about the כהנים who brought a ram as an אשם, and says it shows they had all been with שפחות חרופות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says the men agreed to send away their wives and brought a ram as a guilt offering. רב חסדא says this teaches that all of them had been with designated maidservants.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חסדא explains a פסוק in עזרא. He says it shows that these men had been with שפחות חרופות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The only sin where a person brings an אשם for forbidden relations is a שפחה חרופה. So if the פסוק says they brought an אשם, רב חסדא concludes that this must have been their sin. It ties the story in עזרא to the law we have been learning.

keyTerms.meaning: guilty ones; it hints at bringing a קָרְבַּן אָשָׁם (guilt offering)
a ram from the flock, the animal brought for this אָשָׁם
designated maidservants: maidservants set aside (engaged) for a slave

steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the special אשם for a שפחה חרופה also appears outside the תורה, in a real historical story.

phrases.english: "And they gave their hand to send away their wives,
phrases.notes: עזרא 10:19

phrases.english: and being guilty, a ram of the flock for their guilt."
phrases.notes: A ram is exactly the אשם brought for a שפחה חרופה, and that is the clue רב חסדא uses.

phrases.english: Rav Chisda said:
This teaches that all of them
had relations with designated maidservants.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁכּוּלָּן שְׁפָחוֹת חֲרוּפוֹת בָּעֲלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the discussion of the man's אשם by showing an example of it in נ״ך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The ram brought as an אשם by the כהנים in עזרא shows that they had all been with שפחות חרופות.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: a ברייתא reads 'redeemed' and 'not redeemed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's question about which שפחה is meant. It brings a ברייתא that plays the two words 'והפדה' and 'לא נפדתה' against each other.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה asked: which maidservant? The ברייתא says: 'and redeemed' could mean fully redeemed, so the פסוק says 'not redeemed.' But that could mean not redeemed at all, so the פסוק says 'and redeemed.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes a ברייתא that notices the פסוק seems to say both 'redeemed' and 'not redeemed.' This sets up the next step, which explains how both can be true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word blocks a wrong reading of the other. 'והפדה' alone would mean fully redeemed, and 'לא נפדתה' alone would mean not redeemed at all. Together they point to something in between.

keyTerms.meaning: so the פסוק teaches us by saying

phrases.english: Which is the maidservant, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
"And redeemed": might it mean all of her?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20

phrases.english: The verse says: "not redeemed."
Might it mean she was not redeemed at all?
The verse says: "and redeemed."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: defining the שפחה from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק's words 'redeemed' and 'not redeemed' each limit the other, so she is neither fully redeemed nor fully unredeemed.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא: half maidservant, half free, engaged to a Hebrew slave
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how she can be both redeemed and not redeemed. רבי עקיבא answers that she is half שפחה and half free, and engaged to an עבד עברי.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can this be? She is redeemed and not redeemed. Half of her is a maidservant and half is free, and she is engaged to a Hebrew slave. These are the words of רבי עקיבא.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks how both words can be true. רבי עקיבא answers that she is partly freed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being half-free makes both words literally true: part of her was redeemed and part was not. The man she is engaged to is an עבד עברי, a Jewish slave.

keyTerms.meaning: how so? How can both be true?
half maidservant and half free woman

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'redeemed and not redeemed' as a contradiction. For רבי עקיבא both are true at once, because she is half-free.

phrases.english: How so?
Redeemed and not redeemed:
half of her is a maidservant and half of her is a free woman,
and she is engaged to a Hebrew slave.
These are the words of Rabbi Akiva.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the tension set up by the two words in the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How can she be both redeemed and not redeemed?
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: She is half-maidservant and half-free, engaged to an עבד עברי.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל: a full Canaanite maidservant
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל disagrees. He says the פסוק is talking about a regular שפחה כנענית, engaged to an עבד עברי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ישמעאל says: the verse speaks of a Canaanite maidservant who is engaged to a Hebrew slave.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל gives a different definition. For him she is a full maidservant, not half-free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees with רבי עקיבא that the man is an עבד עברי. The argument is only about the woman's status: fully a שפחה, or half-free.

keyTerms.meaning: a non-Jewish (Canaanite) maidservant who is fully owned

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael says:
The verse speaks of a Canaanite maidservant,
and she is engaged to a Hebrew slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר: בְּשִׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית הַכָּתוּב מְדַבֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opposing view to רבי עקיבא on who the woman is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שפחה is a full שפחה כנענית, engaged to an עבד עברי.

steps.title: Then why the double wording?
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל raises a question on his own view: if she is a full שפחה, why does the פסוק say 'redeemed, not redeemed'?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, why does the verse say 'and redeemed, not redeemed'?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל himself asks how to explain the extra word 'והפדה,' since for him she was never redeemed at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי עקיבא used both words. If רבי ישמעאל says she is fully unredeemed, the word 'והפדה' seems to have no job.

keyTerms.meaning: if so, if that is true
why does the פסוק need to say?

phrases.english: If so, why does the verse say:
"and redeemed, not redeemed"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבי ישמעאל raises a question on his own reading.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ישמעאל's view that she is a full שפחה כנענית
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If she was never redeemed, the word 'והפדה' seems pointless.

steps.title: The Torah speaks the way people speak
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל answers that the double wording is just normal human speech and does not teach anything new.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah spoke in the language of people.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי ישמעאל defends his view. The repeated words are just a normal way of talking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי ישמעאל, 'והפדה לא נפדתה' just means 'she was not redeemed at all,' said with emphasis the way people talk. So there is no hint of a half-free woman.

keyTerms.meaning: the Torah spoke the way people normally speak, so extra words don't always teach something new

steps.whatToRemember: רבי עקיבא: half-free, engaged to an עבד עברי, learned from both words. רבי ישמעאל: a full שפחה כנענית; the double wording is just דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a famous general rule of רבי ישמעאל that shows up all over ש״ס: not every extra word in the תורה comes to teach a new law.

phrases.english: The Torah spoke in the language of people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge against רבי ישמעאל.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Interpretive principle: the repeated words are ordinary speech, not a source for a new law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The double wording must mean she is partly redeemed.
steps.terutzMaskana: The double wording is just emphasis, so she can be a full שפחה כנענית.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה: the half-free case is the one left over
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says all forbidden relations are spelled out elsewhere, so this פסוק must be about the one case left: a half-free woman engaged to an עבד עברי.
steps.simpleTranslation: All forbidden relations are spelled out for us. What is left for us is a woman who is half maidservant and half free, engaged to a Hebrew slave.
steps.whatsHappening: A third תנא gives his view. He agrees with רבי עקיבא's case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reasons from the leftover case: every other forbidden case is already covered, so this פסוק must be about the half-free woman. As step 32 explains, he also uses 'והפדה לא נפדתה': since 'כי לא חופשה' already says she is unfree, those extra words must teach that she is half-free.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya says:
All forbidden relations are spelled out for us;
what is left over for us is
one who is half maidservant and half free woman
and engaged to a Hebrew slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה אוֹמֵר: כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת מְפוֹרָשׁוֹת לָנוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A further view that matches רבי עקיבא's case, using a different line of reasoning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שפחה חרופה is a half-free woman engaged to an עבד עברי, since every other forbidden case is already spelled out.

steps.title: אחרים: a Canaanite maidservant engaged to a Canaanite slave
steps.stepSummary: אחרים learn from 'לא יומתו כי לא חופשה' that she is a שפחה כנענית, engaged to an עבד כנעני.
steps.simpleTranslation: Others say: 'They shall not be put to death because she was not freed.' The verse speaks of a Canaanite maidservant, engaged to a Canaanite slave.
steps.whatsHappening: A fourth opinion. אחרים say both the woman and the man are Canaanite slaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They hold she is a full שפחה כנענית, and they read 'והפדה לא נפדתה' as ordinary speech. As step 34 explains, they apply 'כי לא חופשה' to the man, teaching that he too is not free. Unlike everyone before them, they say the man is an עבד כנעני, not an עבד עברי.

keyTerms.meaning: they shall not be put to death

steps.whatToRemember: Four views on the שפחה חרופה: רבי עקיבא and רבי אלעזר בן עזריה say half-free, engaged to an עבד עברי. רבי ישמעאל says a full שפחה כנענית, engaged to an עבד עברי. אחרים say a שפחה כנענית, engaged to an עבד כנעני.

phrases.english: Others say:
"They shall not be put to death because she was not freed":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20

phrases.english: the verse speaks of a Canaanite maidservant,
and she is engaged to a Canaanite slave.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲחֵרִים אוֹמְרִים: לֹא יוּמְתוּ כִּי לֹא חוּפָּשָׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a fourth opinion that changes who the man she is engaged to is.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The שפחה חרופה is a שפחה כנענית engaged to an עבד כנעני.

steps.title: Where does רבי ישמעאל learn that she is engaged to an עבד עברי?
steps.stepSummary: The double wording 'והפדה לא נפדתה' fits רבי ישמעאל's view, but the גמרא asks where he gets the detail that her fiancé is an עבד עברי.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רבי ישמעאל, 'redeemed, not redeemed' is fine, because the Torah talks the way people talk. But he also said she is engaged to an עבד עברי. Where does he learn that?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts one part of רבי ישמעאל's view and asks for the source of a second part. It is setting up an answer that will come in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Back in step 26, רבי ישמעאל already explained the double wording. That only proves she is a regular שפחה. It does not tell us who her fiancé is, so the גמרא asks for a source for 'engaged to an עבד עברי'.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense / granted (this part is fine, but...)
The Torah speaks the way people normally speak
Engaged (in the first stage of Jewish marriage)
A Jewish servant who works for a set time
From where do we know this?

phrases.english: According to Rabbi Yishmael, it makes sense
why it says 'and redeemed, not redeemed'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20

phrases.aramaic: כִּדְקָתָנֵי: דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: as he taught: the Torah spoke in the language of people,
but what he taught, that she is engaged to a Hebrew slave,
from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי ישמעאל's view from steps 24 and 26 to look for the source of its second detail.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק source showing that, for רבי ישמעאל, her fiancé is an עבד עברי.

steps.title: 'כי לא חופשה' shows that he is free
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says 'she' was not freed. That implies the man is in some sense free, which fits an עבד עברי.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'because she was not freed.' That means he was freed, so he must be an עבד עברי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 29 with a careful reading of the words 'כי לא חופשה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק stresses that only she is not free. From that we infer that he is free. An עבד עברי is a free Jew who only owes work for a time, so he fits that description.

keyTerms.meaning: By implication / from this we can infer

phrases.english: As it is written: 'because she was not freed,'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20

phrases.english: which implies that he is free.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the man she is engaged to.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the source question of step 29.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: From 'כי לא חופשה': only she is unfree, so he is free, meaning an עבד עברי.

steps.title: Isn't רבי אלעזר בן עזריה saying the same as רבי עקיבא?
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's conclusion (a half-free woman engaged to an עבד עברי) is the same as רבי עקיבא's, so why is he listed separately?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה says exactly what רבי עקיבא says!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא for listing two opinions that seem identical.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 27, רבי אלעזר בן עזריה said the פסוק is about a half-free woman engaged to an עבד עברי. That is the same case רבי עקיבא described. A ברייתא should not repeat the same opinion twice under two names.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה הַיְינוּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא!
phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya is the same as Rabbi Akiva!
phrases.notes: רבי עקיבא's view, from earlier in the ברייתא, is also a half-free woman engaged to an עבד עברי.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה הַיְינוּ רַבִּי עֲקִיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from רבי ישמעאל to the next opinion in the ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's listing of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה as a separate opinion.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Same conclusion as רבי עקיבא, so there is no reason to list him separately.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is answering רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: He agrees with רבי ישמעאל that the Torah usually talks like people, but argues that here the extra words must teach something: a half-free woman.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is talking to רבי ישמעאל: 'I agree with you that usually the Torah talks like people. But here it's different. The פסוק already says "she was not freed," so why add "redeemed, not redeemed"? It must come to teach about a woman who is half שפחה and half free.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's view is listed separately because he reaches רבי עקיבא's result by a different path, aimed at רבי ישמעאל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike רבי עקיבא, he accepts the rule 'דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם' in general. He only says it doesn't apply here: 'כי לא חופשה' already tells us she is unfree, so 'והפדה לא נפדתה' would be pure repetition. Extra words must teach something, so they teach that she is half free.

keyTerms.meaning: Half maidservant and half free woman

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה does not reject 'דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם'. He agrees with it in general and only says it doesn't fit here, because the פסוק already said she is not free.

phrases.english: He is speaking to Rabbi Yishmael:
As for me, in general I hold like you
phrases.notes: Literally 'he holds', but he means himself.

phrases.english: that the Torah spoke in the language of people,
but here it is different.

phrases.aramaic: מִכְּדֵי כְּתִיב לֵיהּ קְרָא: ״כִּי לֹא חוּפָּשָׁה״,
phrases.english: Since the verse already wrote 'because she was not freed,'
why do I need 'and redeemed, not redeemed'?
Learn from it that it comes for this,
for a woman half maidservant and half free.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Same conclusion, different reasoning and audience
steps.terutzHavaAmina: His view is just a repeat of רבי עקיבא.
steps.terutzMaskana: He accepts רבי ישמעאל's general rule but shows the extra words here are needed, since 'כי לא חופשה' already says she is unfree.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a ברייתא lists two sages separately when their reasoning differs, even if their final case is the same.

steps.title: Where do אחרים learn that he is an עבד כנעני?
steps.stepSummary: אחרים also hold that the Torah talks like people, which explains the double wording, but where do they learn that her fiancé is an עבד כנעני?
steps.simpleTranslation: For אחרים, 'redeemed, not redeemed' is fine, because they also say the Torah talks like people. But where do they learn that he is an עבד כנעני?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to אחרים and asks for the source of their detail about the man. It is setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28, אחרים said she is a full שפחה engaged to an עבד כנעני. The double wording is explained by 'דברה תורה כלשון בני אדם', but nothing yet shows that the man is an עבד כנעני.

keyTerms.meaning: He holds / he is of the opinion

phrases.english: According to Aḥerim, it makes sense why it says 'and redeemed, not redeemed,'

phrases.aramaic: קָסָבַר: דִּבְּרָה תּוֹרָה כִלְשׁוֹן בְּנֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: since they hold: the Torah spoke in the language of people,
but this, that he is a Canaanite slave, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallels step 29, now for אחרים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source for אחרים that her fiancé is an עבד כנעני.

steps.title: 'כי לא חופשה' is moved over to teach about him
steps.stepSummary: We already know she is not free, so 'כי לא חופשה' is not needed for her. It is applied to him instead: he too is not free, meaning an עבד כנעני.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'because she was not freed.' If we don't need it to teach about her, use it to teach about him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers step 33. It takes words that seem extra about the woman and uses them to teach about the man.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אחרים, the פסוק already makes clear that she is a full שפחה, so 'כי לא חופשה' adds nothing about her. Using the rule 'אם אינו ענין', the words are applied to him, teaching that he is also unfree: an עבד כנעני. This reads the same words the opposite way from רבי ישמעאל in step 30.

keyTerms.meaning: If it is not needed for this matter

steps.whatToRemember: The same words 'כי לא חופשה' teach opposite things: for רבי ישמעאל the man is free (an עבד עברי), and for אחרים the man is a slave (an עבד כנעני).

phrases.english: The verse says: 'because she was not freed,'
if it is not needed for her,
apply it to him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Through 'אם אינו ענין', 'כי לא חופשה' is applied to the man: he is not free, so he is an עבד כנעני.

steps.title: משנה: Who is exempt or liable in עריות
steps.stepSummary: In all עריות, a minor is exempt and a sleeping person is exempt. Someone who sins by accident brings a חטאת, and someone who sins on purpose gets כרת.
steps.simpleTranslation: In all forbidden relationships: if one person is an adult and one is a minor, the minor is exempt. If one is awake and one is asleep, the sleeping one is exempt. If one did it by accident and one on purpose, the accidental one brings a חטאת and the deliberate one gets כרת.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lays out a general rule for every case of עריות, judging each person separately.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each partner is judged on his or her own state: age, awareness, and intent. Being a minor or asleep exempts completely. Acting by accident leads to a חטאת, and acting on purpose leads to כרת. This general rule for עריות sets up a contrast with the special laws of שפחה חרופה that this סוגיא has been discussing.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the start of a new משנה)
A sin offering brought for an accidental sin
Spiritual cutting off, the heavenly punishment for some sins done on purpose

phrases.english: MISHNA: In all forbidden relations,

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד גָּדוֹל וְאֶחָד קָטָן – קָטָן פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: if one is an adult and one a minor, the minor is exempt;

phrases.aramaic: אֶחָד עֵר וְאֶחָד יָשֵׁן – יָשֵׁן פָּטוּר,
phrases.english: if one is awake and one asleep, the sleeping one is exempt;
if one acted unwittingly and one intentionally,
the unwitting one brings a sin offering and the intentional one is punished with karet.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the discussion of the ברייתא ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In עריות each person is judged separately: a minor or a sleeping person is exempt, an accidental sinner brings a חטאת, and a deliberate sinner gets כרת.
steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the basic rule for liability in עריות, which the סוגיא will compare with the different rules of שפחה חרופה.

steps.title: Is a minor liable with a שפחה חרופה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה's wording implies that a קטן would be liable with a שפחה חרופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: And here, with a שפחה חרופה, is a minor liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and challenges the משנה. By saying 'in all עריות a minor is exempt,' the משנה seems to suggest that in the case of a שפחה חרופה the minor is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A קטן is never punished by the Torah for anything. So the implied contrast, that he would be liable here, cannot be correct. The גמרא needs to find a different way to read the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
A minor, who is not yet obligated in מצוות
Liable, meaning he gets a punishment or must bring a קרבן

phrases.english: Gemara:
And here, is a minor liable?
phrases.notes: 'Here' means the case of a שפחה חרופה, which this משנה is about.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges an inference from the משנה rule quoted in step 35.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wording 'in all עריות a minor is exempt'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording implies that a minor is liable with a שפחה חרופה, but a minor is exempt from every Torah punishment.

steps.title: Here even the adult is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה rereads the משנה: in other עריות only the minor is exempt, but with a שפחה חרופה even the adult partner is exempt, because their punishments are linked.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is what the משנה teaches. In all עריות, if one partner is an adult and one is a minor, the minor is exempt and the adult is liable. But here, even the adult is exempt. Why? Because the two of them are linked together in the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question. The contrast in the משנה is not about the minor at all. It is about the adult partner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ordinary עריות, each partner is judged on his or her own, so the adult is still punished even when the other partner is a minor. With a שפחה חרופה, the man's אשם and the woman's lashes are joined together in one פסוק, so one partner cannot be punished without the other. If one of them is a minor and exempt, the adult is exempt too.

keyTerms.meaning: They are compared to each other, meaning their laws are linked

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the key principle of the סוגיא: with a שפחה חרופה, the man's and the woman's liability depend on each other.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת, אֶחָד גָּדוֹל וְאֶחָד קָטָן –
phrases.english: In all forbidden relationships, if one is an adult and one is a minor,
the minor is exempt and the adult is liable;
but here, the adult is also exempt.
What is the reason?
Because they are compared to each other.
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20–21: her lashes and his אשם appear together in the same פסוקים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 36 by rereading the משנה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה implies that a minor is liable with a שפחה חרופה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The contrast is about the adult partner: with a שפחה חרופה even the adult is exempt, because the two partners are linked.

steps.title: Is a sleeping person liable with a שפחה חרופה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the same challenge about the משנה's rule that a sleeping person is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: In all עריות, if one partner is awake and one is asleep, the sleeping one is exempt. So here, is the sleeping one liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה and raises the same kind of challenge as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone who is asleep did nothing on purpose, so it makes no sense to punish him or her. Yet the משנה's wording again seems to suggest that a sleeper is liable with a שפחה חרופה.

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת, אֶחָד נֵיעוֹר וְאֶחָד יָשֵׁן – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: In all forbidden relationships, if one is awake and one is asleep, he is exempt.
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה. 'He is exempt' means the one who is asleep.

phrases.english: And here, is the sleeping one also liable?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel challenge to step 36, applied to the sleeping person.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's wording 'one awake and one asleep, he is exempt'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wording implies that a sleeper is liable with a שפחה חרופה, which is unreasonable.

steps.title: Here even the awake partner is exempt
steps.stepSummary: Using the same reasoning, רב יהודה in the name of רב explains that with a שפחה חרופה even the awake partner is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said in the name of רב: This is what the משנה teaches. In all עריות, if one partner is awake and one is asleep, the sleeper is exempt and the awake one is liable. But here, even the awake one is exempt. Why? Because they are linked together in the פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the same kind of answer as step 37, applied to someone who is asleep. The contrast is about the partner who is awake.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the man and the שפחה חרופה are punished as a linked pair, if one of them was asleep and is exempt, the other one is exempt as well.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means to teach (a rereading of the text)

steps.whatToRemember: With a שפחה חרופה, if either partner is exempt (because of being a minor or being asleep), both are exempt, since their punishments are linked in the פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, הָכִי קָתָנֵי:
phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said in the name of Rav: This is what it teaches:

phrases.aramaic: כׇּל עֲרָיוֹת, אֶחָד נֵיעוֹר וְאֶחָד יָשֵׁן –
phrases.english: In all forbidden relationships, if one is awake and one is asleep,
the sleeping one is exempt and the awake one is liable;
but here, even the awake one is exempt.
What is the reason? Because they are compared to each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב, הָכִי קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 38 the same way step 37 answered step 36.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה implies that a sleeper is liable with a שפחה חרופה.
steps.terutzMaskana: With a שפחה חרופה even the awake partner is exempt, because the two are linked.

steps.title: A ברייתא that treats different cases alike
steps.stepSummary: A תנא recites a ברייתא before רב ששת: the חכמים treated finishing the act like beginning it, acting on purpose like acting without intent, the normal way like the unusual way, and being awake like being asleep.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב ששת: They made someone who completes the act like someone who only begins it; someone who intends like someone who does not intend; the normal way like the unusual way; and someone awake like someone asleep.
steps.whatsHappening: A new source is brought in. It lists four pairs of cases that the חכמים treated the same way, and it sets up רב ששת's challenge in the next steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא does not say which law it is talking about. That missing detail is exactly what רב ששת will question.

keyTerms.meaning: One who completes the act of relations
One who only begins the act (the first stage)
In the normal way / in the unusual way

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav Sheshet:
phrases.notes: A תנא here means someone whose job was to recite ברייתות from memory.

phrases.english: They made one who completes like one who begins;
one who intends like one who does not intend;
the normal way like the unusual way;
one who is awake like one who is asleep.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא that also deals with being awake and being asleep, which was the topic of step 39.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים treated four pairs of cases as equal: completing and beginning, intending and not intending, the normal way and the unusual way, and awake and asleep.

steps.title: With a שפחה חרופה, completing is not like beginning
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת objects: if the ברייתא is about a שפחה חרופה, finishing the act and only beginning it cannot be the same, since only finishing brings liability.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said to him: What are you saying? If you are teaching this about a שפחה חרופה, why did they make completing like beginning? With a שפחה חרופה, one who completes the act is liable, but one who only begins it is not liable!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת attacks the first pair in the ברייתא, assuming that it is talking about a שפחה חרופה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a שפחה חרופה, the Torah gives liability only for a completed act, unlike other עריות, where even beginning the act brings liability. So saying the two are 'the same' does not fit a שפחה חרופה.

keyTerms.meaning: A maidservant designated (engaged) to a man

phrases.english: He said to him: What are you saying?
If you are teaching about an espoused maidservant,
why did they make one who completes like one who begins?
One who completes with an espoused maidservant is liable,
one who only begins is not liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the first pair of the ברייתא from step 40.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement 'they made one who completes like one who begins'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With a שפחה חרופה, liability comes only from completing the act, so completing and beginning cannot be treated the same.

steps.title: With her, intending is not like not intending
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת adds a second objection: the שפחה חרופה is liable only if she acted on purpose, so intending and not intending are not the same.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: How can they make intending like not intending? If she intended it, she is liable. If not, she is not liable!
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds a second challenge to the same ברייתא, this time against the second pair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The שפחה חרופה gets lashes only if she acted willingly. If she did not intend it, she is not punished. So her intention clearly matters, which goes against the ברייתא's claim that it makes no difference.

keyTerms.meaning: She intends it, meaning she acts willingly

phrases.english: And furthermore: one who intends like one who does not intend?
If she intends it, she is liable;
phrases.notes: Her liability here is lashes, as the פסוק says 'בקרת תהיה.'

phrases.english: if not, she is not liable!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against the same ברייתא, this time against its second pair.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's statement 'one who intends like one who does not intend'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The שפחה חרופה is liable only when she acts willingly, so intention does matter.

steps.title: Normal way and unusual way are not equal with a שפחה חרופה
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת's third objection: with a שפחה חרופה only relations in the normal way bring liability, because the פסוק says 'שכבת זרע.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And also, 'the normal way is like the unusual way' does not fit. With a שפחה חרופה, a man is liable for the normal way and not liable for the unusual way. What is the reason? The פסוק says 'שכבת זרע.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת adds another objection to the ברייתא. If it is about a שפחה חרופה, the clause 'the normal way is like the unusual way' cannot be true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the חכמים treated the normal way and the unusual way the same. But for a שפחה חרופה the פסוק uses the words 'שכבת זרע,' which point to relations that can lead to children, meaning the normal way only. So with her the two ways are clearly not equal.

keyTerms.meaning: Lying with seed: the פסוק's words for the act with a שפחה חרופה

phrases.english: And also, 'the normal way like the unusual way':
phrases.notes: This quotes the third pair from the ברייתא in step 40.

phrases.english: in the normal way, with a שפחה חרופה, he is liable,
and in the unusual way he is not liable.
What is the reason?
It is written 'lying with seed'!
phrases.notes: ויקרא 19:20

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third objection in רב ששת's series against reading the ברייתא as about a שפחה חרופה
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's clause 'the normal way like the unusual way,' read as being about a שפחה חרופה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק's words 'שכבת זרע' limit liability with a שפחה חרופה to the normal way, so the two ways cannot be equal.

steps.title: What could 'awake like asleep' mean?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת's fourth objection: the clause 'awake like asleep' also does not fit a שפחה חרופה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what is the meaning of 'awake like asleep'?
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת finishes his list of problems by challenging the last clause of the ברייתא, 'awake like asleep.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person who is asleep is exempt, since what happens is out of his control. So it is hard to see how being awake could be treated the same as being asleep here. With this, all four pairs fail to fit a שפחה חרופה.
steps.whatToRemember: All four pairs in the ברייתא (finishing and beginning, on purpose and not on purpose, normal and unusual, awake and asleep) are NOT equal for a שפחה חרופה. So the ברייתא does not seem to be about her.

phrases.english: And what is 'awake like asleep'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final objection in רב ששת's series; together they reject the שפחה חרופה reading
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A sleeping person is exempt, so being awake and being asleep cannot be equal in this case.

steps.title: Trying other forbidden relationships: finishing like beginning?
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת tries reading the ברייתא as being about other עריות, and right away questions the clause 'finishing like beginning.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the ברייתא is teaching about other forbidden relationships, how did they make one who finishes like one who begins?
steps.whatsHappening: Since the ברייתא does not fit a שפחה חרופה, רב ששת tries a new reading: maybe it is about the other עריות. He immediately raises a problem with the first clause.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the other עריות, even just beginning the act (מערה) already makes a person liable. So the new idea there is that beginning counts like finishing. Saying 'they made finishing like beginning' sounds backwards, and this phrasing problem is what the גמרא is pointing at.

keyTerms.meaning: One who only begins the act

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two readings. With a שפחה חרופה, only finishing makes one liable. With other עריות, even beginning makes one liable. The problem here is only that the ברייתא's wording seems backwards for other עריות.

phrases.english: And if it teaches about the other forbidden relationships,
did they make one who finishes like one who begins?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the שפחה חרופה reading fails, רב ששת tests a new reading and challenges it right away
steps.kashyaTarget: The clause 'finishing like beginning,' read as being about other עריות
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: With other עריות, beginning already brings liability, so the new idea is that beginning is like finishing. Saying 'finishing like beginning' does not fit.
